name: Shahr-i Sokhta
description: Shahr-i Sokhta, the "Burnt City," is a vast mudbrick ruin in the desert of Sistan and Baluchistan in southeastern Iran, beside the Helmand River. Founded around 3200 BC, it grew into a Bronze Age hub on trade routes across the Iranian plateau, with separate quarters for monuments, homes, workshops and burials. Dry desert air has kept its buildings and artefacts remarkably well preserved.
